lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: PRESS RELEASE: MegaBun is thrilled to announce the Bake-Off Showdown, a celebration of bread-adjacent excellence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A letter signed 'a concerned customer': 'Their entry is a cake designed by committee. It has eleven layers and no opinions.'

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Don't count the layers, dear. Count the smiles. A good cake is a conversation, not a spreadsheet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Judges' orders are on the counter. The Contest Mixer is humming. Make the town proud.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The committee cake has sagged into something that resembles a hat. The crowd votes with its forks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: PRESS RELEASE: MegaBun congratulates itself on a record-breaking participation trophy.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Well! Frosting like that, I'd have given you the recipe for free.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: MegaBun's cake wins by a nose, mostly because it leans on the judge's table.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: PRESS RELEASE: MegaBun takes full credit for the town's baking spirit. The town takes the leftovers home.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: They won the ribbon. You won the crowd's second helpings. I know which I'd rather have.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: MegaBun has opened a stall across the harbor. A giant sign reads: ARTISANAL FAIR EXPERIENCE™.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Buns-A-Lot, in a very warm bun costume, hands out coupons for 3% off.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A letter from a concerned customer: 'He's going to try 4% by lunch. Please hold the line. P.S. Your scones are incredible.'

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Every customer you fill is one who walks over here. Warm samples beat coupons every time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By afternoon the queue at MegaBun's stall is a single man holding a 6% coupon and a deep sense of doubt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Buns-A-Lot quietly removes his costume head, wipes his brow, and takes a sample of your tart.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Never mock the intern. Feed him. He's the only one over there who knows what bread is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: MegaBun's stall wins the afternoon with a 9% coupon and a bouncy castle shaped like a bun.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The customers drift back anyway, clutching coupons and craving something that tastes like the 1990s.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: They came for the coupons and stayed for the cake. That's the order I'd prefer, but I'll take either.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The judges have arrived at the town square. One of them is, unmistakably, Chad Crustworth's mother.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: PRESS RELEASE: MegaBun's samples will arrive microwaved in their original packaging, in the interest of authenticity.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Three plates, three judges. Make each one better than the one before.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Tasting Table is open. High-tier orders only today.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The final judge puts down her fork and says, with some ceremony, 'Chad would be so proud. Of you.'

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Chad is reported to be 'reviewing the feedback' for several days.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: A mother's vote is the only one that can't be bought. Frame that scorecard.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: MegaBun's samples win a round on the strength of the packaging. The judges are mostly worried about the plastic.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Chad's mother votes for you anyway. It isn't enough, but it is noted.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Two out of three judges can be wrong. It happens. Three out of three, never.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: MegaBun has bought every sack of flour in town. A press release calls this 'a supply chain synergy opportunity'.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Flour Mill is running slow. A cease-and-desist letter arrives, politely, about 'unauthorized baking'.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Under the third floorboard, dear. I always kept a little something put by.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Grandma's Secret Stash is yours for the duration. Use it wisely.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: MegaBun's lawyers send a second letter. It begins 'We regret to inform you that your baking is lovely.'

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Flour Mill is back to speed and humming. Somewhere a warehouse of flour sits, unloved and unsold.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: They bought the flour. They can't buy the knowing what to do with it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: MegaBun's warehouse gets all the flour and, apparently, no one to bake with it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Their lawyers send a third letter. It contains a recipe for 'artisanal bread product', with a typo in the word bread.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: We'll manage. We always have. Pass me the second-best flour and I'll show you what I mean.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The town is raising money for the lighthouse. MegaBun has pledged a single, enormous novelty check.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is the size of a door. It is, famously, signed in a colour marker that does not appear on any bank's list.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: A lighthouse is just a very tall way of saying 'we haven't forgotten you'. Let's keep it lit.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Bake Sale Table is set. Every order helps.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The check is presented at the square with great ceremony. It bounces, audibly, off the stage.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You raise more than the posted amount. The lighthouse is lit by evening, and it is a very good lighthouse.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Money is just crumbs. It's the baking that fills the plate.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The check clears, narrowly, and the lighthouse gets its repairs. MegaBun puts out a press release about it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everyone agrees the town's cake did most of the actual work. The press release does not mention the cake.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: A lit lighthouse is a lit lighthouse. We still had the better bake sale.
